title: Pill — The box measures. Pill explains.

slides.name: Title

els.text: CAL HACKS 13.0 · IDEA TO DEMO · FIGMA
A $40 lab-in-a-box. One tablet, about three minutes, one of three answers. In a clinic, that answer decides whether the supplier gets paid.
Art · the site’s binary pill (pill.js), captured from pill-site.vercel.app

slides.notes: Pill is a forty-dollar box. One quarter tablet, about three minutes, two channels that must agree. It says three things only: PASS, NEEDS LAB, UNABLE TO VERIFY.

slides.name: The moment

els.text: THE MOMENT · DELIVERY D-1042 · REPLAY TM-02
The bottle says vitamin B2. The blue line drops into the reference band, so a one-sensor tester would call it a pass. The green glow never moves.
Illustration · the shape of replay TM-02, redrawn; not live sensor data.
RULE N2 · INLINE MOVED, GLOW DID NOT RISE
A one-sensor tester would have passed it.
POLICY P2 · HOLD, DRAFT THE LAB REFERRAL

slides.notes: This bottle says vitamin B2. Inside is chalk. The blue line drops right into the reference band, so a one-sensor tester would call that a pass, but the green line never moves. Pill says NEEDS LAB and the supplier's four hundred and eighty dollars stays held, lab referral drafted. Sandbox money; this is a replay, and we say so.

slides.name: The problem

els.text: WHO estimates 1 in 10 medical products in low- and middle-income countries is substandard or falsified. The lab instrument that catches one costs $20,000 to $100,000.
Illustration · one tablet in ten. WHO, 2017: substandard and falsified products counted together.
extra malaria deaths a year in sub-Saharan Africa, modelled central estimate, from substandard and falsified antimalarials (range 64,000–158,000)
children's deaths linked to contaminated cough syrups in three countries, 2022–23, most under five
spent each year on substandard and falsified medical products, by WHO's estimate

slides.notes: WHO estimates 1 in 10 medical products in low- and middle-income countries is substandard or falsified. A new lab dissolution tester costs twenty to a hundred thousand dollars, and lab results take seven to ten business days. A clinic pharmacist has neither; what they have is an invoice to pay this afternoon.

slides.name: The idea

els.text: Lot numbers can be copied. Dissolution cannot.
A recall lookup trusts the label. Pill measures the tablet itself: one tablet in 900 mL of water, a paddle at the same speed every run, two light sensors watching it dissolve.
A 465–475 nm LED shines across the cup. Riboflavin absorbs it as the tablet dissolves.
A second sensor behind green plastic sees riboflavin glow. Chalk clouds the water; it does not glow.
Fig 1 · the station, drawn in code for the site (station.js) and captured from pill-site.vercel.app: box, cup, paddle, blue LED, two sensors, ESP32, touchscreen.

slides.notes: Riboflavin absorbs blue and glows green. Chalk only blocks light. Two channels must agree, so a cloudy cup cannot pass on its own; the ESP32 measures and decides nothing.

slides.name: How a run works

els.text: The app draws the run as a pill filling to last night’s reference plateau (ten reference runs make the band). At 100% the curve has flattened and the seven rules run.
0:20 · dark, then blank. Lid open? No run.
0:40 · one tablet in. The paddle turns.
Blue light fades as the tablet dissolves.
3:00 · seven rules, in order. The rule that fired is printed.
Illustration · example levels; the app draws them live from the sensor stream.

slides.notes: One quarter tablet, about three minutes. The pill fills to last night's reference plateau; at 100% the seven rules run in order and the rule that fired is printed. Claude explains the result in plain English but never sets a verdict.

slides.name: Three answers

els.text: Seven rules, checked in order. A model writes the plain-English “why”; it never sets the verdict.
Plateau in the reference band and the glow rose with it (P1).
Light dropped with no glow, no plateau, or a plateau outside the band (N1–N3).
No reference for this drug, a fault, or too little data (U1–U3).

slides.notes: It says three things only: PASS, NEEDS LAB, UNABLE TO VERIFY. Never a fourth. PASS means this tablet's curve matched last night's riboflavin references on this box; it does not mean right drug, right dose or contaminant-free.

slides.name: Clinic mode

els.text: A clinic samples one tablet from each delivery. The policy agent reads the verdict, the recall check and the spend cap, and proposes. Only a pharmacist’s tap releases money.
pays into escrow when the delivery is logged
holds it until a PASS and a pharmacist’s tap
+ the pharmacist’s tap → escrow pays the supplier (P1)
held; the lab referral is drafted with the curve (P2)
escalated to a person; no money moves (P3)

slides.notes: And it decides the money. A policy agent holds the payment in escrow and proposes release only on a PASS; a pharmacist taps to approve. Claude explains the result and keeps the log, but never sets a verdict and never moves money. Sandbox and testnet money today.

slides.name: Coinbase

els.text: The server answers “Payment Required”: 0.05 USDC on Base Sepolia.
The buyer’s wallet signs that exact payment; over its spend cap, it refuses.
The facilitator settles it on Base Sepolia. TESTNET USDC only.
The server answers with the verdict and the rule id that fired.
Escrow → supplier in USDC, only after PASS and a pharmacist’s tap.
No local reference? Buy a verdict from another station over x402, capped per day.
Every station can sell /verify to other clinics.

slides.notes: Other clinics can buy a verdict for five cents over x402: the server answers 402, the wallet signs, the facilitator settles, and the server answers 200 with the verdict and the rule id. Testnet USDC on Base Sepolia; nothing here is real money.

slides.name: App screens

els.text: One app: the touchscreen and the phone.
20 routes in React. All 296 app screenshots go into the Design file, one frame each, labelled with their route. These twelve are the newest pass.

slides.notes: One web app on the station's touchscreen and on any phone. These are the newest build pass; the Design file has every screenshot, grouped by pass and linked to its route.

slides.name: Six phases

els.text: The app follows the station’s own state machine. Each phase has its own time, its own look and its own check; a failed check stops the run and says why.
LEDs off. The box must read dark; a light leak means the lid is open, and the run stops.
Plain water, paddle on. The blank must hold steady (CV under 2 %) or it retries, up to 3 times.
It waits for the inline reading to fall 6 %. After 30 s the screen prompts.
The pill fills, the curve falls, the glow rises. Glow flat while blue falls: the amber moment.
Flat for 20 s (|dA/dt| < ε) means plateau. No plateau by 180 s: timeout.
Seven rules, in order. The rule that fired is printed with the word.

slides.notes: A run is six phases, the same ones the station walks through. Lights off for three seconds: the box must be dark, or the lid is open and nothing runs. Ten seconds of clear water as the blank; it must be steady. Drop the tablet; the station waits for the reading to fall six percent. Dissolving: the pill fills and the glow should rise with it. Settling: twenty flat seconds is a plateau. Then the seven rules give the word.

slides.name: Gemini checker

els.text: Gemini checks what the sensor says.
After the run, Gemini reads the label, looks at the cup and checks for a recall, then compares that with the sensor. Six steps, each logged with its own time.
The sensor decides. The checker explains and never changes the word. A pharmacist or doctor decides.

slides.notes: After the run, a Gemini agent checks what the sensor says: it reads the label, looks at photos of the cup, checks openFDA for a recall, cross-checks expiry, drug and lot, and compares what the camera saw with the sensor numbers. Every step is logged with its own time. The verdict word comes from the sensor and is never changed. The follower is the same Gemini, docked on every screen, answering questions about what is on it.

slides.name: Website

els.text: Built code-first (Vite + anime.js) after a 16-persona panel scored a plain, honest page 8.0 against a copied storytelling site at 3.7. Words stay ink; colour lives in backgrounds and lines.
Hero · the binary pill, drawn in characters by pill.js
Fig 3 · three answers, the same screen as the app
Payments · the verdict is the invoice

slides.notes: The website came first and set the tokens the app inherited. A 16-persona panel picked a plain, honest page over a copied storytelling site. All three crops are the live site today, captured headless.

slides.name: Workflow

els.text: Code first, then Figma from the code.
Honest order: no Figma was used Friday or Saturday morning. The Figma files are generated from the repo, and the log says so.

slides.notes: We are a code-first team. Ideation and prototyping happened in markdown, AI panels and HTML. Figma enters as the place the repo is published to: slides, screens, tokens and the ideation board.

slides.name: Design from code

els.text: screenshots · CSS :root · debate JSON · stage log
Node, no npm deps; ffmpeg for images
slides, pages and board in one file
the loop: Figma styles and variables → Composio → CSS back in the repo

Recipe for code-first teams: keep the repo as the source of truth, emit one JSON, let a plugin draw it. One run gives designers editable layers, every screen, the tokens as styles, and a board of how you decided.
Why a plugin: the Figma REST API and our Composio connector can read, comment and set variables, but cannot create layers or slides. The Plugin API can.

slides.notes: The REST API cannot draw, so the repo emits deck.json and a one-file plugin draws it in Slides, Design or FigJam. Composio closes the loop: comments, dev resources back to the code, thumbnails, and tokens back to CSS. Nobody has run it in real Figma yet; that step is marked pending.

slides.name: Stage log

els.text: 16 AI personas per panel, reference study; FigJam board generated after
One model played all 16: agreement inflated (SD 0)
binary-pill.html, phone mock in the site’s JS; Figma Make prompt written
Nobody could click it without a code editor
CSS :root copied site → app; Figma styles + variables; Composio → CSS
8 of 27 tokens arrived identical; no record of intent
Claude Code + 3 parallel builders; Pill → Figma plugin
P6 hold rule bug; double deploy; REST API can’t draw
PENDING = the Figma step is written but not yet run; its minutes and rating stay blank in the log, not estimated.

slides.notes: Four stages, timed from git commit times. Steps not yet run in real Figma say pending; we do not estimate them. The full log, with the Figma Make prompt and a ten-minute reproduce box, is STAGE-LOG.md.

slides.name: What broke

els.text: The scaffold held money only when the recall lookup was unreachable, so a delivery with no bottle attached could be proposed for release.
Caught by a builder’s end-to-end test.
A `tail -6` cut off Vercel’s output, the deploy looked unfinished and was re-run: two identical production deploys.
Read the whole log before re-running.
The Figma REST API and our Composio connector read, comment and set variables. Neither can create a layer or a slide.
So the repo emits deck.json and a plugin draws it.
8 of 27 tokens survived the hand copy
Site → app by hand: 8 identical, 7 changed value, 12 renamed or dropped. Nothing recorded which changes were meant.
Tokens now go to Figma as variables and back as CSS.

slides.notes: What broke, honestly. A rule bug the tests caught, a deploy we ran twice because the output was cut off, an API that cannot draw, and a hand-copied palette where most tokens drifted. Each one changed how we work.

slides.name: Before and after

els.text: 20 slides × 20 min + 404 screenshots × 1 min + 43 tokens × 1 min = 847 min
Per-unit minutes are our assumption, not a measurement.
repo → deck.json + deck.html, cold build on this machine (2.3 s this run). Plugin logic on a stub Figma API: 6 ms Slides · 13 ms Design · 2 ms FigJam.
Plugin run in real Figma: [fill after running]
bars to scale · after = cold build time
Every run places 404 screenshots (296 app, 108 site) and turns 43 CSS variables into Figma styles and variables, with no hand work. By hand, 8 of 27 site tokens reached the app unchanged.

slides.notes: Before numbers are estimates and say so. After numbers are measured on this machine; the real Figma run time is printed by the plugin and goes into LINKS.md.

slides.name: What PASS does not mean

els.text: The dissolution curve of this one tablet, on this box, was consistent with last night's riboflavin reference runs. No red flags found.
That the tablet is the right drug, the right dose, or free of contaminants. Pill has one reference drug today. Anything it cannot compare goes to a lab, by design.
Results charts on our site are marked as an illustration until the calibration runs are on the page.

slides.notes: Say the limits before a judge asks. One reference drug, riboflavin; anything else is UNABLE TO VERIFY, by design. We never call a medicine good or bad.

slides.name: Tracks

els.text: this deck, the plugin, the stage log
Microsoft · Built for the Real World
the plain-English why; can only downgrade

slides.notes: One build, many judges; only the emphasis changes. Money is SANDBOX or TESTNET on every track.

slides.name: Ask and next

els.text: Ten riboflavin reference runs and chalk runs, plotted on the site in place of the illustration.
Each new drug needs its own band. Until then it is UNABLE TO VERIFY, on purpose.
A procurement officer samples one tablet per delivery; we log every decision and every override.
Ask: try to make it say PASS on the chalk. Then tell us which tablet to calibrate next, and introduce us to one clinic pharmacist.

slides.notes: Our ask: try to make it say PASS on the chalk. Then tell us which tablet to calibrate next, and introduce us to one clinic pharmacist. Everything still pending is marked pending in the repo.

rows.label: What we did
cells: Nine ideas considered, six through scored panels. FloodToll, DripGuard and Payout died on buildability or business. Lot beat Bill and Streets 13 votes of 16 and became Pill. A second panel scored a plain, honest website 8.0 against a copied storytelling site at 3.7.

The prototype was the product. The site's phone mock loops calibration, bottle, recall, run, verdict and release; those loops became APP-PLAN's twelve screens. The binary pill was tried as one HTML file before it went on the site. The clickable Figma prototype (Welcome → Run → NEEDS LAB → held → Pay) is generated by the plugin from the shipped screens, so it always matches the code; link: [fill after running].

The site's 27 tokens seeded the app's palette. The plugin puts the app's colour tokens into Figma as styles and variables, and the script reads them back as CSS, so a change made in Figma can land in code.

The app (20 routes), the x402/Nessie payment service and the Claude and Gemini wiring were generated against written plans. Then the repo generated its Figma: build-deck.mjs turns screenshots, site art, CSS tokens, debate JSON and this log into deck.json; the plugin draws the Slides deck, the Design pages and the FigJam board.

rows.label: What broke
cells: Plain-page scores had a standard deviation of 0: sixteen voices, one opinion. Two persona replies failed to parse. Nothing visual existed; the FigJam board was built from the JSON afterwards, not used live.

Nobody without a code editor could change or click through the prototype; the Figma Make prompt is written to fill that gap. The site went through four versions in 53 minutes; v4 moved colour off the words.

By hand, 8 of 27 tokens arrived identical, 7 changed value (some on purpose: verdict colours re-pointed at mint, amber, grey) and 12 were renamed or dropped. Nothing recorded which changes were intended. Composio's Figma tools read, comment and set variables but cannot draw a layer.

The scaffold's P6 rule held money only when the recall lookup was unreachable, so a delivery with no bottle attached could be proposed for release; a builder's end-to-end test caught it. A tail -6 cut off Vercel's output, the deploy was re-run, and we got two identical production deploys. The REST API cannot create nodes, hence a plugin.
